$contrastPairsDescription: P5.5 semantic-pairing manifest. Every surface token that hosts text, icons or borders is declared here with its paired foreground and the WCAG 2.1 level that applies: 'text' 4.5:1, 'largeText'/'ui' 3:1, 'disabled' reported only (1.4.3 exempts disabled controls). Read by scripts/check-contrast.mjs (npm run contrast:check). $-prefixed keys are skipped by build.mjs and the Tokens Studio exporter, so this manifest never reaches generated CSS/SCSS/TS or Figma. Chart series ramps, decorative gradients and orb canvas colors are deliberately absent: they are data-viz/brand color, not text or essential UI. Chart axis/legend/tooltip pairs ARE listed because they carry text.

space.$description: Spacing scale — the token name IS the pixel value. 4px grid at 16px and above; 2px half-steps (2/6/10/14) below it. Decision recorded in DESIGN_AUDIT.md P1-5.

radius.$description: Corner radius scale — the token name IS the pixel value. Concentric language: 16 outer surfaces, 12 nested, 10 controls, 8 chips/menu items, 4 micro-marks, full for pills. Pick a role token from component.* when one exists.

shadow.$description: Softer, humane elevation — depth comes from hairline + tint, not heavy drops

scrollUp.$description: shadow.sm mirrored upward. The one use is an overlay footer casting onto a body that is scrolled beneath it (P6-2); a downward shadow there would point away from the content.

buttonInset.$description: Top-edge sheen on filled buttons — light surfaces only. On dark, a light inset reads as a glow, so the dark theme uses shadow.dark.sm instead.

dvOrbitMic.$description: P5.5: the Orbit mic button's periwinkle glow, migrated out of dv-tokens.css. A brand accent glow rather than generic elevation, which is why it is its own shadow token; shadow.dark.dvOrbitMic is the dark counterpart.

zIndex.$description: Stacking-order scale for hand-rolled overlays. Documents the layers already in use; does not change any stacking order. Vuetify components (VMenu, VTooltip, VDialog, etc.) compute their own z-index internally — the dropdown/modal entries below record those defaults for reference only and must never be used to override Vuetify's own overlays.

dropdown.$description: Vuetify VMenu/VTooltip default — do not override in CSS, this value is for documentation/reference only

modal.$description: Vuetify VDialog default — do not override in CSS, this value is for documentation/reference only

toast.$description: DvToastStack notification layer, above all overlays (.dv-toast-stack)

motion.$description: Motion system — durations, easings, and stagger step for the confident-editorial evolution

background.$description: Cool blue-tinted off-white page canvas — calm professional neutral

surface.$description: Pure white card surface — floats above neutral canvas

surfaceVariant.$description: Neutral light grey — table headers, hover tints

surfaceTint.$description: Very subtle blue tint for soft cards / hover

onSurfaceVariant.$description: A11Y-003: darkened from #737373 to a cool-neutral step so secondary text clears 4.5:1 on surfaceVariant/background/surface (5.35/5.85/6.33:1)

primary.$description: Picton blue, darkened to 5.2:1 on white so filled buttons and links meet WCAG AA. Do not lighten below #0079B5 (4.5:1).

surfaceOverlay.$description: WP-F1: explicit overlay token (menus/popovers/modals) — matches the value mp-theme-aliases.css previously synthesized from surfaceBright

scrim.$description: WP-F1: explicit scrim token — matches the value mp-theme-aliases.css previously synthesized as rgba(textPrimary, 0.32)

outline.$description: P5.5-12: the strong-boundary role — Vuetify's outlined form-field border (settings-form.scss), the composer pill's hover edge and the journey flow arrowhead. WCAG 1.4.11 applies at 3:1 because a field's border is the only thing that makes it perceivable at rest. Was #d4d4d4 (neutral.300) = 1.37:1 on canvas. Neither neighbouring ramp step works: neutral.400 #a3a3a3 still fails at 2.33:1, neutral.500 #737373 overshoots to 4.38:1 and visibly heavies up every field. #8a8a8a is the lightest neutral gray with margin over the floor (3.19:1 on canvas, 3.45:1 on surface), so the Flowbite-style hairline stays as light as compliance allows. Decorative card and divider edges are NOT this token — they use outlineVariant / border / borderSubtle and are unchanged.

borderSubtle.$description: 1px dividers on surface — cool slate hairline that recedes behind content

textMuted.$description: Cool muted text — slate-tinted, slightly higher contrast than #737373

textSecondary.$description: P5.5: light counterpart of color.dark.textSecondary — the light/dark foreground sets are symmetric so mp-theme-aliases.css is a 1:1 map, not a patch table

textDisabled.$description: P5.5: light counterpart of color.dark.textDisabled. Distinct from textMuted (they were previously indistinguishable in light theme). Disabled text is WCAG-exempt (1.4.3) — report-only in check-contrast

surfaceRaised.$description: P5.5: light counterpart of color.dark.surfaceRaised (was synthesized in mp-theme-aliases.css from surfaceBright)

buttonDisabled.$description: Fill of a disabled button. Aliases interactiveDisabled; declared separately so it can carry a foreground partner, which is what Vuetify's hardcoded 26%-alpha disabled styling never gave it (P6-15).

onButtonDisabled.$description: Label of a disabled button. Meets 3:1 against both the disabled fill and the overlay surface it sits on, so a disabled action stays findable in a modal footer, and stays visibly lighter than textMuted so it still reads as disabled.

onSurface.$description: P5.5 semantic pairing: the declared primary ink for the whole same-polarity surface ladder (background, surface, surfaceVariant, surfaceTint, surfaceBright, surfaceOverlay, surfaceRaised, surfaceSunken, interactive*). Convention: Material-style on<Surface>, matching onPrimary/onSurfaceVariant/on*Container

onSurfaceMuted.$description: P5.5 semantic pairing: the declared secondary/muted ink for the surface ladder

primary.$description: Primary AI actions — 5.0:1 on white text

primaryHover.$description: Hover state for AI primary buttons

primaryActive.$description: Pressed/active state for AI primary buttons

gradientTo.$description: Avatar and chrome gradient end. P5.5: darkened from #0E8FA8 — the old value carried a "4.6:1 with onAccent" claim that measured 3.81:1. Now 4.74:1 with onAccent.

soft.$description: Soft AI background — rationale cards, pill hover

textPrimary.$description: AI emphasis text on light surfaces

textSecondary.$description: AI helper and muted text — 5.1:1 on white

aiMetric.$description: Da Vinci draft metric delta states

flowLogic.$description: Journey builder logic/filter category — violet, distinct from the blue/green/amber flow palette

container.$description: Soft logic tint — icon tiles, hover washes

moduleTile.$description: AUD-L02 ledger — categorical tile-accent palette for ModuleLandingPage quick-action / child-page cards. Eight decorative hues let a tile grid read as visually distinct categories; the `color` prop on QuickAction/ChildPage picks one per call site (blue|violet|rose|green|amber|cyan|indigo|teal) — hues are arbitrary categorical differentiators (not fixed to one meaning or module). Each hue pairs an `accent` (icon-tile foreground before color-mix) with `ink` (darker shade for hover/focus-ring tint). See color.dark.moduleTile for the lightened dark-surface counterparts.

mist.$description: P5.5: darkened from #8499AF. Used as the color of the Orbit hint, muted message and echo text (12-13px), which measured 2.73:1 on dv.orbit.surface; now 4.62:1. Blue-slate hue preserved.

blue.$description: P5.5: darkened one step from #1B9FE0. It fills the Orbit typing caret and the chip hover border — both essential UI indicators under WCAG 1.4.11 — and measured 2.76:1 on dv.orbit.surface. Now 3.08:1.

muted.$description: P5.5: darkened from #94A3B8 (2.34:1 on mutedBg). This is the orb mark's dim/error state ink — a graphical object conveying state, so it takes the 3:1 minimum. Now 3.26:1.

fogTint.$description: P5.5: the diffusion fog tint (dv-diffusion.css) — a near-white haze layered at low alpha over the Da Vinci experience backdrop.

blue.$description: Blue accent ramp — compact dashboard style

surface.$description: L1 card surface — Material dark elevation overlay logic: the canvas→card step is the largest (≈8% white over canvas) so cards read as distinct containers, not the same fill

surfaceVariant.$description: L1-nested surface — table headers, grouped controls, hover wash

error.$description: AUD-L05: lightened one step from #EF8176 so danger text clears the plan's 5.06:1 target on surfaceOverlay (now 5.11:1 on #32373E) after the cool-neutral ladder re-space

surfaceBright.$description: L3/L4 overlay surface — menus, popovers, modals, drawers. Ceiling is set by danger text staying ≥4.5:1 on this fill.

borderTableRow.$description: Repeating row separators — lightest overlay of the divider set so stacked rows don't add up to a grid

borderDividerMuted.$description: Card / menu horizontal dividers — Material dark uses a low-alpha white overlay so the line lifts only slightly off whichever surface tier hosts it. An opaque mid-grey here reads as a hard rule.

fogTint.$description: P5.5: dark counterpart of the diffusion fog tint.

sidebar.$description: Sidebar-specific palette — faint grey shell containing white cards on main canvas

textMuted.$description: P5.5: darkened from #737373 (4.16:1 on sidebar.bg) to clear 4.5:1 body text (now 5.60:1).

textFaint.$description: P5.5: was rgba(115,115,115,0.62) = 2.23:1 on sidebar.bg. Faint is still text, so it now resolves to an opaque step clearing 4.5:1 (4.72:1).

chart.$description: Multi-series chart palette — single-hue Picton Blue ramp (well-spaced steps)

heatmapInk.$description: P5.5: ink for heatmap/matrix cells whose fill is a LIGHT tint. Heatmap fills are produced by tintHex(), which mixes toward white in both themes, so the cell ink is a function of the fill's luminance, not of the theme — a theme-following ink rendered light-on-light in dark mode. Picked at runtime by readableInkOn() in src/plugins/chartPalette.ts.

heatmapInkStrong.$description: P5.5: ink for heatmap/matrix cells at the saturated end of the ramp. Pairs with heatmapInk; see that token for why this is theme-independent.

axisLabel.$description: Axis tick labels — secondary on L1 surface. P5.5: alpha raised 0.55 -> 0.65 so label text clears 4.5:1 on surface (3.95 -> 5.49:1).

grayBlue.$description: Gray + Blue — focal blue with gray de-emphasis and a monochrome blue ramp for multi-series

grayBlueGold.$description: Gray + Blue + Gold — grayBlue with a subtle golden third hue (divergent-accent option)

social.$description: Bright social — royal blue, turquoise, mint on a pale blue base (design 1f)

grayBlue.$description: Gray + Blue (dark) — PROVISIONAL, mirrors light pending dark tuning

grayBlueGold.$description: Gray + Blue + Gold (dark) — PROVISIONAL, mirrors light pending dark tuning

social.$description: Bright social — royal blue, turquoise, mint on a pale blue base (design 1f) — PROVISIONAL dark mirror

grid.$description: Low-alpha overlay grid — decorative, not an essential boundary

fontSize.$description: UI text ramp — the token name IS the pixel value. Every component font-size and every text.* role resolves here. No fractional sizes (DESIGN_AUDIT.md P1-6). Hero sizes above this ramp live in display.*.

heavy.$description: For hero numbers and display-xl moments

snug.$description: Component headings — dialog and drawer titles.

compact.$description: Supporting lines under a heading — subtitles, descriptions.

letterSpacing.$description: Tracking scale — tighten at display sizes

display.$description: Display type scale — Inter only, big/tight/confident. Deliberately its own hero ramp outside the fontSize UI ramp; use for page heroes and marketing surfaces, never for product chrome.

text.$description: Named text roles — the styles product surfaces should actually use. Every fontSize aliases the fontSize ramp; body is 14px (canonical, DESIGN_AUDIT.md P1-2).

label.$description: Form label — the one label spec. A field's static top label (settings-form.scss) and MpFormField's label for composite controls both resolve here, so a wrapped chip group and a plain text field are labelled identically. Line box height is component.field.labelHeight.

component.$description: Component-level role tokens. Each one is a design decision (which primitive this element uses); everything else should reference the primitive scales directly.

control.$description: Shared interactive control height — buttons and form fields align on it (P1-10)

chip.$description: Chip role tokens. One height ramp for every chip in the system (P2-4) — sm|md|lg matches the shared size vocabulary (P2-1).

height.$description: Chip height ramp — sm 20 / md 24 / lg 32. Was 20/22/34px across three unrelated chips.

menu.$description: Action-menu popovers (kebab menus, dropdown-button menus, select/autocomplete option lists — everything inside a v-menu overlay). Menu items are deliberately denser than in-page rows: itemHeight 36 vs listItem.minHeight 40, because a menu is transient chrome, not content (decided 2026-08-31, Atlassian-calibrated). Applied by the global popover rule in global.scss, so select options share the density. minWidth is consumed by explicit components only (MpRowActionsMenu) — never by the global rule, since v-select syncs its dropdown width to the field.

bubble.$description: Chat message bubbles (MpChatBubble): Tickets thread, theme-builder Da Vinci panel, docs assistant. The tail is the bottom corner on the author's side dropping to tailRadius. maxWidth 88% was the majority value across the hand-rolled bubbles it replaced (2026-08-31).

banner.$description: Full-width edge strip (MpBanner). minHeight 44 sits between control.height 40 and the table row floor 48 — proven by PlgTrialBanner before extraction (2026-08-31).

segmented.$description: Segmented control (MpSegmentedControl): padded track + pill segments. itemHeight = height − 2×padding, every number on a scale stop. md track = control.height (40) so a segmented control and a button align on one baseline; sm (32) is for dense chrome (builder bars, menu rows). Geometry proven by the app-bar theme switcher before extraction (2026-08-31).

card.$description: Card role tokens. `padding` is THE card inset — 20px, matching MpKpiCard and the dashboard widget family so P4-1 inherits it. Compact/Spacious are the only sanctioned escape hatches; a card that needs a fourth value is a design bug, not a token gap.

dialog.$description: Dialog / overlay geometry. One header-body-footer rhythm: MpDialog owns it and MpFormDrawer shares it, so a modal and a drawer cannot drift apart (P4-6). Was five different inset sets across eight raw v-dialog implementations.

headerGap.$description: Gap between the header's lead icon, heading block and trailing controls. Split from footerGap in P6-1: they were the same 8px, but one is a header rhythm and the other an action-row rhythm, and a shared name meant tuning one silently moved the other.

headerMinHeight.$description: Floor for the header band, so a title-only modal and a title+subtitle modal are the same height (P6-1). It was 72 / 87 / 109px depending on which optional lines were present. A floor, not a cap: an eyebrow header grows past it.

width.$description: Dialog max-width ramp — sm|md|lg matches the shared size vocabulary (P2-1).

drawer.$description: Right-side drawer geometry. Everything else about a drawer (padding, gap, radius, header rhythm) is component.dialog.* — a drawer and a modal are one object seen from two sides. Only the width ramp differs, because a drawer is sized against the viewport edge rather than centred.

width.$description: Drawer width ramp — sm|md|lg matches the shared size vocabulary (P2-1). Replaces a free-form `width: number` that had grown to eight values between 420 and 680 (P6-4). md is the default and keeps every previously-unset drawer at its rendered width.

wizard.$description: Full-page wizard shell (MpWizardShell). measure.* is the centred content column of the scrollable body: sm is the canonical single-column form measure, md fits wider form/table steps, lg fits split-pane steps (content + sticky preview) and galleries. Replaces six free-form widths (780/820/880/920/1040/1160) that had grown across the create flows.

listItem.$description: List-row geometry. minHeight reuses component.control.height so a list row, a button and a form field all sit on one 40px baseline (P1-10).

field.$description: Form-group spacing. Stated once here so label→control, control→control and control→hint are identical in every drawer, dialog and settings page.

sectionGap.$description: Space around a section heading inside a form (MpFormSection). One value for every occurrence; it was seven hand-rolled heading patterns each carrying their own mb-2/mb-3/mb-4 (P6-9).

height.$description: Field box ramp, mapped from Vuetify's density prop: compact=sm, comfortable=md (the theme default), default=lg. md references control.height so a field, a button, a toolbar control and a list row share the 40px baseline — the old +2px boxPadding (44px box) was retired with the static-top-label rework.

labelHeight.$description: Line box of the static top label (13px text.label). Headroom above a labelled field = labelHeight + labelGap; MpFormGrid derives its trailing-action offset from the same pair.

state.$description: Empty / error / placeholder state geometry. One shape for every "nothing to show here" surface — MpEmptyState owns it, MpErrorState and SettingsPlaceholder compose it.

table.$description: Data-table geometry. Row height is a decision here, not a side effect of padding + line-height — the header row used to render ~22px against ~48px body rows (P4-4). headerMinHeight reuses component.control.height so a table header, a nav item, a button and a form field share one 40px baseline.

toolbar.$description: Data-table toolbar. Its own height token: borrowing layout.appbarHeight coupled every table toolbar to app-shell chrome (P4-5).

nav.$description: Navigation-specific decisions component.listItem.* does not cover. Item height, padding and gap come from listItem — there is deliberately no second nav sizing scale.

builder.$description: In-layout builder asides (journey builder inspector etc.) — in-flow panels that reserve canvas width, deliberately narrower than the modal drawer ramp (drawer.width.sm 440 would starve the canvas). Named here so the width stops being a stray literal (GAPS §9).

widget.$description: Dashboard-widget action overlay only. Widget INSETS come from component.card.* — this is deliberately not a second inset pair (see the Phase 3 follow-up). The clearance a bespoke header needs is derived from these three so it cannot drift from the overlay again (P4-2).

drawerWidth.$description: Legacy alias for the drawer md stop. Kept because the Storybook `measure` scale binds it; new code should reach for component.drawer.width.* directly.

formMaxWidth.$description: Reading measure for a centred single-column form body inside a builder (CreatePromotion). Long-form settings pages use the full content width instead.

inboxListWidth.$description: Conversation-list pane of a master-detail inbox (Service Tickets). Distinct from component.builder.panelWidth on purpose: an inspector aside and a list pane should be able to move independently.

inboxRailPanelWidth.$description: Expanded panel beside the inbox's icon strip (Customer info / Tags / Orders). The strip itself is space.48.

breakpointSplit.$description: Viewport below which a master-detail split shows one pane at a time. Equals Vuetify's md threshold so useDisplay().mdAndDown agrees with the CSS. Sass-only, like breakpointCompact: $mp-layout-breakpointSplit.

breakpointCompact.$description: The one viewport where overlays collapse to their compact inset and drawers go full-bleed. Media queries cannot read CSS custom properties, so this is consumed as the generated Sass variable $mp-layout-breakpointCompact, never as var().
